standard_prerequisites.use: Jacobian-ness of the punctured spectrum of a local Noetherian ring (Properties, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson), the isolated-point fibre criterion for quasi-finiteness (Algebra, lemma-isolated-point-fibre), and openness of the quasi-finite locus (Algebra, lemma-quasi-finite-open).

core_obligations: Pick a closed point of the punctured spectrum inside the prescribed open.
Verify quasi-finiteness at the point and extend to a principal localization.

proof_roadmap.step: Jacobson punctured spectrum supplies the prime q.
Isolated fibre point plus localization gives the quasi-finite map.

difficulty_reason: For a local map of local rings A -> B, essentially of finite type with A Noetherian and the residue field extension finite, any open V of Spec B containing a prime not lying over the closed point of A contains a prime q, not meeting the closed point of A, such that A -> B/q is a localization of a quasi-finite ring map. The retained proof is written: B is Noetherian; the punctured spectrum of B is Jacobson (Properties, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson) so a closed point q can be chosen inside the nonempty open cut out from V by removing primes over m_A; the two-point spectrum of B/q plus the isolated-point criterion (Algebra, lemma-isolated-point-fibre) show finite type A-algebra C presenting B/q is quasi-finite at the corresponding prime, and Zariski's open locus for quasi-finiteness (Algebra, lemma-quasi-finite-open) finishes after a principal localization. Retained author proof at lines 14969-14991.

dedup.scope: Existence of a quasi-finite closed slice meeting a prescribed nearby open.
